Helps users get clearer error text and non-misleading help examples for these wallet RPCs

result.summary: This PR fixes three small wallet RPC issues: an error message in listtransactions that referenced an argument by its outdated name, a bare 'Invalid parameter' error in listsinceblock that didn't name the failing argument, and a misleading sendmany help example that appeared to set a confirmation count via an ignored dummy parameter. Each fix is a separate commit with an accompanying functional test update. Two earlier commits touching deprecated argument metadata were dropped after maintainer feedback that such changes should either be a proper deprecation cycle or not touched at all.
result.problem: Wallet RPC users see confusing or unhelpful error messages (referencing stale argument names or giving no argument name at all) and a sendmany help example that teaches a no-op, making debugging and correct usage harder.

resolved_concerns: maflcko questioned modifying near-dead deprecated-argument code; author agreed and dropped those two commits rather than expanding scope.

categories.rationale: P4 because these are cosmetic fixes to error message wording and help text, not to actual RPC behavior. The sendmany example fix does correct a genuinely misleading example ('passing a value in the minconf position... taught a no-op' per commit message), which is a minor documentation-correctness win, but none of the three changes affect fund safety, correctness of RPC results, or any real user workflow beyond clearer error text.

uncertainties: Whether the sendmany example was actually confusing anyone in practice, versus just a theoretical correctness issue, is not evidenced by outside complaints.
result.card: This PR makes three small wording fixes to wallet RPCs: naming the skip argument correctly in a listtransactions error, naming the failing argument in a listsinceblock error, and fixing a sendmany help example that misleadingly implied setting a confirmation count via an ignored parameter. Each fix has a matching functional test update and is a separate, reviewable commit. The author dropped two earlier commits after maflcko argued that touching near-dead deprecated-argument code without a real deprecation cycle wasn't worthwhile, leaving the PR narrowly scoped to genuine wording bugs. No open objections remain and the state is Positive. This is purely cosmetic/documentation-level cleanup with no fund-safety, correctness, or performance impact, so it ranks P4 in wallet.
